analysis.title: Shift4 Payments (FOUR): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Weaker than expected preliminary 2027 guide weighs on stock
key_insights: Shares underperformed after the company lowered FY26 guidance and gave a 2027 outlook of mid to high single digit revenue growth, versus prior commentary GS believes had indicated closer to HSD-LDD growth.

GS reads management as taking a more proactive and prudent approach to guidance, citing uncertainty in the tax-free shopping business (Japan, France, Middle East), ongoing headwinds from deprecation of legacy revenue streams, and weaker same-store sales dynamics.
After a stream of guidance reductions over the last year, GS calls FOUR a show-me story until the company shows stabilizing fundamental performance.
On updated estimates, shares trade at roughly 12x EV/Unlevered FCF for 2027. GS says an inflection in growth or better FCF conversion would likely be needed for a rerating.
3Q26 gross revenue was $1,319mn vs Visible Alpha consensus of $1,331mn. Gross revenue less network fees was $648mn, in line with consensus.
End-to-end volume was about $61bn, 6% below expectations. Net take rate was about 0.66%, even with the Street.
Gross margin before D&A was 71% vs 72% consensus. Gross profit before D&A was $459mn, 2% below consensus.
Adjusted EBITDA was $310mn, 1% above expectations, at a 48% margin vs 47% expected. Adjusted EPS was $1.49, 10% above consensus.
FY26 guidance was lowered on revenue, EBITDA and EPS. End-to-end payment volume is guided to $240bn-$250bn vs consensus of about $251bn.

FY26 net revenue is guided to $2,450mn-$2,460mn. Adjusted EBITDA is guided to $1,110mn-$1,130mn, about 0.5% below consensus at the midpoint. Adjusted FCF is guided to about $465mn-$475mn (about 42% conversion), about 3% above consensus at the midpoint. Non-GAAP EPS is guided to $5.05-$5.15.
GS stays Neutral and cuts its 12-month price target to $43 from $47, based on about 8x EPS-SBC on Q5-Q8 estimates (multiple unchanged). The stock was $44.82, implying 4.1% downside.

GS cut adjusted diluted EPS estimates for 2026/2027/2028 to $4.66/$5.90/$6.86 from $5.05/$6.05/$7.51. Revenue estimates for 2027 and 2028 fell to $2,612.7mn and $2,752.8mn from $2,751.2mn and $3,030.3mn.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $43 from $47 on lower EPS estimates after reduced FY26 guidance and a weaker preliminary 2027 outlook. Rating stays Neutral.

FY26 company guidance (lowered): end-to-end volume $240bn-$250bn (consensus about $251bn), net revenue $2,450mn-$2,460mn, adjusted EBITDA $1,110mn-$1,130mn, adjusted FCF about $465mn-$475mn, non-GAAP EPS $5.05-$5.15.
Management's preliminary 2027 outlook points to mid to high single digit revenue growth, below prior commentary GS believes was closer to HSD-LDD growth.
GS estimates (forecast): adjusted diluted EPS 2026E $4.66 (from $5.05), 2027E $5.90 (from $6.05), 2028E $6.86 (from $7.51). GS 2026E revenue $2,452.1mn, 2027E $2,612.7mn, 2028E $2,752.8mn.
risk_factors: Downside risks: weaker macro, worse than expected execution against recent M&A, higher competition.
Upside risks: better than expected FCF conversion, better cross sell of end to end solutions, improving macro backdrop.
Uncertainty around the tax-free shopping business (Japan, France, Middle East), deprecation of legacy revenue streams, and weaker same-store sales.
